scope: Resolve an omitted PostgreSQL B-tree key collation from an ordinary text column declared with absolute stock C, including a session temporary table and an ordinary unmodified LIKE copy.
rules: Keep the exact declared stock C collation on its physical text slot while preparing a complete table declaration. Keep it on an unmodified copy of that slot.
A text key without a COLLATE clause selects its declared collation. When the declared collation is stock C, omission and an explicit absolute C yield the identical completed key and operator class.
The indexed column's actual declaration controls collation inheritance. Another column, schema, table copy, search-path shadow, or earlier catalog phase cannot supply a substitute.
An explicit stock C on the index key overrides any declared collation. Unresolved or separately named collation choices belong to the wider obligation ledger.
Copy and phase facts are used during construction. Keep only the selected key collation and bound field in completed IR. Text INCLUDE positions and text NULL tests do not acquire a key collation.
negative: The desired text column has a database default, POSIX, or an unresolved unqualified declaration
A neighboring field declares C while the indexed text field's collation is unknown
Another ordinary table at the same name on the search path declares C
A collated text key does not admit an unrelated operator class
observations: Exact owner and operand coordinates, ordered comparison roles, qualified collation and operator class, and identical graph on direct and analyzed construction
Native index metadata and result order and values for the original and generated SQL, including NULL and case-distinct values
Distinct registration and typed refusal when no supported inherited collation can be determined
faults: Forget the earlier column collation when copying the table
Bind a different physical slot's collation
Treat an unresolved inherited collation as stock C
